account.md pass 4: the pass 3 text kept as account-p3.md (sha256 matched); the last section now has a paragraph 'The cuts, and the rule that decides whether an element stays'. It says: the model, when built, stated that a process or condition enters only with a grounded arrow, and did not keep it (K01, P06 and R02 stood with no arrow until C5); in this account the criterion written before pass 1 decides whether an element stays, ranking story rooms told with no residue above fewer elements; the arrow rule decides only what the account may say an element brings about; K01 is told by what members did, with no effect claimed, and its one claim beyond presence is F-009. Leg names in that paragraph were replaced by 'the second pass of this account' and 'the third pass', since the readers do not know the leg names. No element, arrow, tier or finding changed.

The handler's point answered in notes-C5.md (pass 4 section) and account.md: the criterion written before pass 1 decides whether an element stays (section 4 sets the count by what keeps composition and explanatory power alive; section 5 asks for the criterion first; item 2 ranks rooms told with no residue above fewer elements). The arrow rule, stated in model-C4.md and broken by the model from C2's first pass (five standing elements with no arrow: P06, K01, C01, C02, R02), now does two things only: it names candidates for a cut, and it limits what the account says of an element with no arrow (what members did; no effect claimed). P06 and R02: no arrow, no telling rested on them, cut at no cost. K01: no arrow, ten told rooms rest on it, kept; its claim beyond presence is F-009. Pass 2's error was using the arrow rule as the decider and reading the rooms after (slip recorded under pass 3). Not a move: no element, arrow or tier changes.

C5b opens (the readers' build). Read AGENT.md, the head, the stage file, diary --last 5, validate.py --open C5 (0 errors, 0 warnings). The passes stopped at pass 4. This leg, by section 8: the run_manifest.json entry; author_claims.jsonl (five to nine claims); three rooms named in notes-C5.md, drawn by query; RETURN-C5.md; three packets under 50 KB with account.md, figure-C5.md, propositions.jsonl and the three rooms through the verbs. The handler's reminders: the readers are the second reader for the declaration prose pass and for my Stigmergy codes (J's ruling 4: the rule and the amended declarations with their members' quotes go into the packets), and the declarations are built from the ledger, not structure-C4.md. Close with done.sh C5 --cut packets-out.

C5b, the three readers' rooms (section 8), rule written before the draw. Facts by query (c5b_room_sizes.py): account.md cites or names 7 early-side rooms and 2 late-side rooms, so the late side is the side it has visited least. Each room is served whole through the verbs (room --no-canvas facts, forest, every quote by cite.py), so the reader judges the whole coded record and not my selection; the 50 KB ceiling, shared with the account, figure and propositions, caps each room's served material at 4,500 bytes. That cap is a limit of the packet, not of the model, and it biases the draw towards small rooms; I say so in the notes. Pools: (1) reached easily: a pass 5 story room told with no residue, not cited or named in account.md, at least 8 coded concepts; (2) the last story could not tell: a pass 5 story room told with a residue (none was untold); (3) the late side: first coded turn after hour 48, not cited or named in account.md, not a story room, at least 8 coded concepts. Each pool is cut to rooms whose material fits the cap, then one room drawn with random.Random(20261015). No room note is opened.

figure-C5.md written (c5b_figure.py, from model/elements.jsonl, model/arrows.jsonl and propositions.jsonl): the C5b draft of the figure as text, section 10. Boxes in three columns (conditions K01, K02; 16 mediators named for what members do; what follows P11, P12, P13), the terminus at hour 73, K01 as a box with no arrow, C01 and C02 beside as claims. 20 arrows, each with its proposition, strength, count against its null and one instance (the first audited transition). Drawing 2 drops the theorised A11 and A12. No loop drawn. What it leaves out: A21, P21, P22, the candidates. It is drawn again at C5d from the model that survives the readers.

C5b, the rooms' rule revised before any room was drawn or opened. Under the first rule no story room fits: whole, the told rooms of pool 1 run from 47 to 307 coded passages and the residue rooms of pool 2 from 12 to 1,276, so no room in either pool was under the 4,500-byte cap (only five late-side rooms were). Each packet holds account.md (10,839 bytes), figure-C5.md (5,032) and propositions.jsonl (19,202) under the 51,200-byte ceiling, besides the instruction and the second reading J's ruling 4 asks for. Revised rule: the same three pools without the cap (floor of 8 coded passages kept for pools 1 and 3), one room per pool drawn with random.Random(20261015); each room served as the facts lines of room --no-canvas and 10 of its coded passages drawn by cite.py's own seeded draw (--grep . --n 10 --seed 20261015), verbatim with their citations. The forest is not served: a drawn room's forest runs to 10 KB or more. The reader is told the passages are a random sample.

author_claims.jsonl written: nine claims I believe account.md makes, each a sentence a reader can agree or disagree with, each tied to its paragraph (c1 the order from start to keeping; c2 the bare answer; c3 the mark tells what is missing; c4 neighbours and agreements without enforcement; c5 the contest and its answers; c6 a template settles a design, decided order rare; c7 hour 73 and curation; c8 where the model does not reach; c9 the rule that decides whether an element stays). Written from account.md alone. Slip: the stage puts the claims first; I drew the three rooms before writing them. The rooms do not bear on the claims.

C5b, the rooms' serving revised a second time, for the ceiling, before any page was opened for content: with 10 passages per room the three packets measured 54,154 to 54,815 bytes against 51,200. Now: 7 passages per room by cite.py's seeded draw (same seed, same three drawn rooms: cardinals, luciomains, mysterydungeon); the facts lines keep everything above the thread list except the forest's summary line, since the forest is not served; the rule's C5a-02 extension is served by its scope paragraph only.
